stem: Meera keeps some dry moong seeds in a jar in her kitchen. After three days on wet cotton, the seeds sprout and tiny roots appear. Why should the dry moong seeds be classified as living things?

options.text: Because seeds are always small, dry and hard objects
Because they came from a plant that was once living
Because under suitable conditions they can germinate and grow into new plants
Because they do not show any change until they are cooked

teacher.key_rationale: A seed is living because, given suitable conditions (water, air, warmth), it germinates and grows into a young plant that can continue the life cycle. Option B is the trap for students who think origin alone decides classification; A and D reflect the surface-feature error that an unsprouted seed is non-living. Key recalculated for the new stem: C.
